newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's AMP wants five percent stake limit.
newsitem.headline: Australia's AMP wants five percent stake limit.

text.p: Australian insurance and pension fund group Australian Mutual Provident Society (AMP) said on Wednesday it would prefer to limit individual shareholdings to five percent for the first five years after its late 1998 demutualisation.
AMP managing director George Trumbull told a news conference after the group's annual meeting that AMP was heading towards offering policyholders shares only rather than a cash or share option.
"Our preference for a cap is for five percent for five years," Trumbull said.
"But at some point in time, subject to the market vagaries, if someone wanted to write a cheque big enough, someone could decide to take over AMP," he said.
He also confirmed AMP chairman Ian Burgess' earlier comments that AMP was not looking to offer itself for sale by tender in the same way that Scottish Amicable did recently.
"We have decided not to aggressively pursue a sale by tender," Trumbull said.
He said a sale by tender was unlikely given AMP's size and the limited number of groups able to swallow such a large chunk.
"Our demutualisation has been pretty well publicised. Anybody with enough money you would have assumed would have heard and would have come out of the woodwork already," he said.
"But I've been around too long to say 'never'," he said.
AMP currently has A$7.8 billion of members' capital and AMP expects profits between now and the float would raise that to about A$9 billion.
The market value, however, would have to include a valuation of the AMP brand, Trumbull said.
"One would argue that the AMP brand has significant value above the A$9 billion," he said.
He said he was confident AMP's demutualisation plan, which is expected to go to a vote of the more than two million policyholders on November 20, would be successful.
"There's always some risk, but we're not very concerned," he said.
